chapter: Emmett Hardy and the river towns
title: Escaping the Algiers feud and playing the Midway
summary: They escape a gang from the river towns, and he describes the Midway, chicken wire and the blues in three tempos.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: So then we finally got out and we were going to catch the streetcars because we were all from over the river. And those days there was always a feud going on between the guys from Algiers and the guys from New Orleans, the guys from Gretna and the guys from New Orleans. Or even from one neighborhood to the other. And always about 15 of them got around us. They wanted to know what we were doing, taking a shorty job and everything like that. And they were just about getting ready to... They'd always send a little guy to pick on you to make you mad, you know, enough to want to fight or get smart and then they'd rap you. And they were just about getting ready to rap us when this little fellow who had told us don't worry about anything comes out from a high box step across the street there. He comes out there and he got a smoke wagon on him about that long and he says, I dare one of y'all to touch him. He says, they got a better band than Sharky's got. You know, one of those things. And we finally got on the streetcar and got home. But we never did go back anymore. And then we had a job at a place over the river called the Midway. And they started playing... The last tune they started playing... They quit at quarter to twelve because you had to quit at quarter to twelve to catch the last streetcar to make the Jackson Ferry, you see. And they started playing the blues at eleven o'clock, you see. And they played the blues for forty-five minutes. They'd play them slow first and then medium tempo. And then what we called fast tempo in those days, not even medium now, you know. And they'd play the blues in those three different tempos. Well, that's when the free falls would start off. And it was an open air place. You see, no, no, it had a roof over it, but all the rest of it was open and had chicken wire in front of the bandstand so the beer bottles wouldn't hit the band. And things like that. And you'd have to fight your way through the fight to get out to get in the streetcar, you know. Oh, they had several of them over there like that. They had that Owls Hall on the river there. But, yeah, it was right just about a half a block down from Jackson Avenue. And a fella coming from New Orleans would come over and try to fool one of the girls there.
